_comment: Mutation testing runs against dist/spec-node (CommonJS, executed by Jasmine in
plain Node) rather than through Karma/Chrome. Two reasons: the Chrome path made
every mutant depend on a browser launch, and the command runner cannot
recompile TypeScript between mutants. Mutating the compiled CJS keeps the
semantics identical (Stryker mutates comparison operators, boundaries and
booleans the same way) while each test run costs ~30ms instead of seconds.
Rebuild with `npm run compile:spec-node` before running, so the mutants are
_tsconfigFile_comment: We mutate already-compiled CJS, so Stryker's TypeScript sandbox rewriting is
unnecessary here — and TypeScript 7 (the Go rewrite) removed
ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson, which that rewriting calls, so leaving it on
crashes Stryker 10.1.1 outright. Pointing tsconfigFile at a path that is not
in the project file set makes the preprocessor find nothing to rewrite and
skip the call. If you ever enable @stryker-mutator/typescript-checker, this
needs a real tsconfig and a Stryker release that supports TS 7.
